en: And so when something new emerges, you get excited and you lean forward and you say, well, can I make it faster?
zh: 所以当新事物出现时，你会兴奋，会向前倾身，然后说，好吧，我能把它做得更快吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Can I build a chip that is better at this work?
zh: 我能造出一块更擅长这类工作的芯片吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you ask the other question is, is there enough of this work to justify building a chip that's better?
zh: 然后你会问另一个问题：这类工作是否足够多，足以证明专门造一块更好的芯片是合理的？

speaker: Unknown
en: So you have two questions, can I and should I?
zh: 所以你有两个问题：能不能，以及该不该？

speaker: Unknown
en: And what we saw with AI was an extremely computationally intensive workload.
zh: 而我们在 AI 身上看到的，是一个计算极其密集的工作负载。

speaker: Unknown
en: Unlike, for example, the rise of ARM processors for cell phones, they weren't computationally intensive, they were power intensive, right?
zh: 不像，举例来说，ARM 处理器在手机上的崛起，它们不是计算密集型的，而是功耗密集型的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown

en: And that was sort of the insight.
zh: 这就是那个洞察。

en: And then it was a long, hard slog.

zh: 在我们进入那段漫长而艰难的苦役之前，Eric，显然对你作为投资人来说，你当时也还不是身处这个 AI 时代，但你看到了一些让你投资的东西，而且我想，你之前并不是芯片投资人，你更多做过的是——而且可能永远不会再是了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the thing is like, well, you should do it again, but like, will you do it again?
zh: 然后问题就变成，好吧，你应该再来一次，但是，你还会再来一次吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I ask myself that all the time.
zh: 我一直问自己这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you actually need some naivete.
zh: 比如你其实需要一点天真。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you need to have...
zh: 比如你需要有……

speaker: Unknown
en: This like, oh, can do attitude and this like naivete around it to attempt it.
zh: 这种「能行」的态度，以及围绕它的天真，才敢去尝试。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like otherwise you just don't do it again.
zh: 否则你就根本不会再做了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I've definitely built up a bunch of scar tissue.
zh: 我确实积累了不少伤疤。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, how much science and technology had to be built, how many innovations, how many times, like, the company was going to come to the brink.

zh: 这真是个很难的问题。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 而且团队,创始团队在上一家就已经在一起了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we had some really clear sort of philosophies on what you should do.
zh: 我们对应该怎么做有一些非常清晰的哲学。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 我们的看法是,如果你要去挑战歌利亚,如果市场里站着一个巨人,比如 NVIDIA 在那个时候就已经是了,那么好一点或者便宜一点不是一个可行的策略。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: They had high margins, so if you come in and even if you're two-thirds the price, they can just cut costs.
zh: 他们有高利润率,所以即使你进来时价格是他们的三分之二,他们也可以直接削减成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: They can just charge less.
zh: 他们可以直接收得更低。

speaker: Unknown
en: They can bundle it.
zh: 他们可以捆绑销售。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: What that means is you have to go out with something way better.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 你必须拿出一个产品,它的价值主张是,即使对方把它免费送出去,好吧,他们也无法竞争。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's sort of one direction of our thinking.
zh: 所以这是我们思考的一个方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the other building off that is we want to do hard things that produce that advantage, right?
zh: 另一个在这一点之上的是,我们想做那些能产生那种优势的难事,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: That we want all that hard stuff within the building because that's under our control.
zh: 我们想把所有那些难的东西都留在公司内部,因为那是我们能控制的。

speaker: Unknown
en: All the other stuff's not under our control, but if we can build something that is so fast nobody else can do it, you can't give away your parts to achieve what we can achieve.
zh: 其他所有东西都不在我们控制范围内,但如果我们能造出快到没人能做到的东西,你就无法靠白送你的部件来实现我们能实现的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then you're onto something.
zh: 那你就找到门道了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the only way to do that in our opinion is radical innovation.
zh: 而在我们看来,做到这一点的唯一方法就是激进创新。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't incremental your way to vastly better.
zh: 你没法靠渐进式改进达到好得多的水平。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what has to be in your control?
zh: 那么什么必须在你的控制范围内?

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to have all aspects of the design.
zh: 你必须拥有设计的所有方面。

speaker: Unknown
en: The implementation, you have to understand the manufacturing, you have to understand every part.
zh: 实现,你必须理解制造,你必须理解每一个部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for us, that meant chip, board, system, software, all the way up to the API.
zh: 对我们来说,那意味着芯片、板卡、系统、软件,一直到 API。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was not easy.

speaker: Unknown
en: That makes it more expensive.

speaker: Unknown
en: It makes it take longer.
zh: 这让时间更长。

speaker: Unknown
en: It means there are more ways to fail there.
zh: 这意味着失败的方式也更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you do radical innovation, there are no vendors waiting for you.
zh: 当你做激进创新时,没有现成的供应商在等你。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you build a chip the size of a dinner plate, you can't go to a catalog and find a heat sink because nobody had ever built one bigger than a postage stamp.

zh: 所以你最终会把大量的时间投入到构建那些支撑你核心业务的东西上,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: The surrounding components.
zh: 那些外围组件。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the result of that is you develop this extraordinary expertise.
zh: 但这样做的结果是,你会发展出这种非凡的专业能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: We didn't start world leaders in packaging.
zh: 我们一开始并不是封装领域的世界领先者。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're right now the best in the world of packaging.
zh: 我们现在是全世界封装领域最强的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We earned it, failure after failure, year after year, until we got it.
zh: 这是我们赢来的,一次又一次失败,一年又一年,直到我们做成了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what you want to do is you want to think about sort of
zh: 所以你要做的是,你要思考

speaker: Unknown
en: How you can innovate across the various elements of the full solution and push as hard as you can.
zh: 你如何在完整解决方案的各个要素上进行创新,并且尽你所能地大力推进。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think like Andrew taught me this in semis and everything else just to like make this like what you need to be shooting for concrete.
zh: 我觉得 Andrew 在半导体和其他方面教会了我这一点,就是把这个东西、把你要瞄准的目标变得具体。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you think of whoever the incumbent is in whatever market, you know, they're getting say twice as good every year in a market like this.
zh: 但今天现有的东西并不是目标,因为如果你看现在市场上的那些公司,

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very dynamic.
zh: 这个市场变化非常快。

en: For a new company to get to scale, to start to get to scale, it's going to take five years at least.
zh: 一家新公司要达到规模、开始达到规模,至少需要五年。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's say with everyone moving as fast as they can, the AI tools, you nail everything, first tape out works, first bring up works, everything goes right five years to get to scale.

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you're basically at two to the fifth, so that puts you at 32x.
zh: 所以你基本上面对的是二的五次方,也就是 32 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you need at least a multiple advantage of that.
zh: 而且你还需要至少超过这个数字的倍数优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you say 3x, so you're basically at 100x.
zh: 所以说 3 倍,你基本上需要 100 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one of the things that happens when you hear a lot about these new ideas is they're like, hey, we're going to be 50% better.
zh: 所以当你听到很多这些新想法时,会发生的一件事是,他们会说,嘿,我们要好 50%。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to be two times as better.
zh: 我们要好两倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what they are, they're like, once we have this design, it's going to be even 10 times better than what exists today.
zh: 但他们说的是,一旦我们有了这个设计,它会比今天现有的东西好上十倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what exists today isn't the target, because if you're looking at the companies that are out there right now,
zh: 但今天存在的东西并不是目标,因为如果你看看现在外面的那些公司,

speaker: Unknown
en: These big companies with a lot of resources are actually doing great work.
zh: 这些拥有大量资源的大公司实际上做得很出色。

speaker: Unknown
en: NVIDIA is advancing the ball materially every year, like very significantly.
zh: NVIDIA 每年都在实质性地推进这项事业,而且推进幅度非常大。

speaker: Unknown
en: NVIDIA and Google and Tranium, they're moving the ball.
zh: NVIDIA 和 Google 还有 Tranium,他们都在推进。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you've got to aim at 100, 500,000 times better if you're going to arrive, if you're going to intersect the market ahead of them.
zh: 所以你必须瞄准好 100 倍、500 倍、1000 倍,如果你想抵达、如果你想在他们之前与市场交汇的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that, just like when you realize that, you're like,
zh: 所以,当你意识到这一点时,你就会说,

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh wait, it can't be small changes in something.
zh: 哦等等,这不可能是某个东西上的小改动。

speaker: Unknown
en: There has to be a very big underlying architectural change, a big thought.
zh: 必须有一个非常重大的底层架构变革,一个重大的思想。

speaker: Unknown
en: There has to be something materially different, whether it's wafer scale, SRAM, whatever it is.
zh: 必须有某种实质性不同的东西,无论是晶圆级、SRAM,还是别的什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those things matter.
zh: 这些东西很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't get there with a collection of modest improvements.
zh: 你不可能靠一堆适度的改进达到那里。

en: Your biggest competitor buys silicon for less than you.

en: You can't run it at Goliath straight on.

zh: 我知道这家公司曾经,你知道的,有过一些濒死经历之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had some near-death experiences.
zh: 我有过一些濒死经历。

en: Pain in my chest when you can't build the thing you're supposed to build.
zh: 胸口疼痛,当你造不出你应该造出来的东西的时候。

en: Yeah.

zh: 还是你根本不知道自己能不能实现技术突破?

en: I think in our space, we were always confident if we could make it, we'd sell it.
zh: 我觉得在我们这个领域,我们一直很有信心,只要我们能造出来,我们就能卖掉它。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are sort of two axes in our life.

speaker: Unknown
en: There is, can you make it?

speaker: Unknown
en: And the other axis is, can you sell it?
